transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Well... I guess what brings me in is that I just keep getting up when I'm really supposed to stay put. Like during client interviews. I'm a private investigator, which everyone thinks is all car chases and glamorous stakeouts, but honestly? It's a lot of sitting across a desk from people while they cry about their spouses. I had this one woman last week, her husband was supposedly at a golf retreat in Florida, but I found out he was actually just two towns over at a... well, anyway, the point is, I couldn't just sit there with her while we talked. I kept popping up out of my chair. 

It happens during these tutoring sessions I do, too. And even my book club! We're reading this historical fiction novel right now, set in the 1920s, and the author gets all the clothing details completely wrong, which drives me crazy because I actually started out as a history major when I was getting my bachelor's before I switched gears entirely. 

But yeah... people are really starting to notice. The women at the book club, my clients, they all give me these looks because I just can't sit and listen. I always end up standing up or wandering around the room when I'm supposed to be sitting down.
Do you often feel restless or have difficulty staying seated, even when you know you should?

Oh, definitely restless. Even if I do manage to force myself to stay in the chair, I'm never actually still. Like when I'm stuck at the computer combing through records, my foot is just bouncing a mile a minute under the desk. Or I'm clicking a pen. I actually had to start buying these specific soft-click pens from this little stationery shop downtown so I don't drive myself crazy. It's right next to this incredible bakery, actually... oh my gosh, they have these almond croissants that are just to die for. I stopped in there last Tuesday when I was working on a background check for this guy who claimed he was a master scuba instructor. Turns out he just took one beginner resort course in Cozumel back in 1998! People will lie about the weirdest things. But anyway, yeah, when I'm looking at those files, I'm shifting around in my seat so much that I completely lose my place in what I'm reading. I have to start the whole paragraph over because I just can't stop squirming.
Do you also find yourself feeling restless or unable to stay seated in situations where you’re not working—like when you’re at home relaxing or spending time with friends or family?

Yeah, it's... it's really not just a work thing. Like, even on days when I don't have any field work and I'm supposed to be relaxing or whatever, I just can't turn it off. I'll be moving from unpacking boxes to reorganizing my case files, and then suddenly I'm running errands like I'm chasing down a hot lead. Which reminds me, I was at the post office yesterday dropping off some documents, and the line was out the door. It's always like that on Tuesdays, I don't know why. You'd think people would go on Mondays, right? But no, Tuesdays are a madhouse. And the postal worker, Dave—I've known him for years, he's got this weird obsession with vintage stamps—he was telling me about this new commemorative set... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, relaxing. Yeah, I just have a really hard time being "off duty." I'm always just... going.
Do you also find it hard to focus or pay attention to details, often making careless mistakes or missing things you're supposed to notice?

Focus? No, not really. I mean, my job is literally all about details, right? If I missed things, I'd be a terrible PI. I'm actually really good at catching the tiny things other people miss. Like, just last month, I was doing this surveillance job—totally routine insurance fraud thing. The guy claimed he had this severe back injury, couldn't lift anything over ten pounds. So I'm parked outside his house in my Subaru—which, by the way, I need to get the oil changed on, the little light keeps coming on and I keep ignoring it because the mechanic I usually go to, Tony, he moved his shop all the way across town and it's just such a hassle to get out there now. Plus, he always tries to upsell me on air filters. It's like, Tony, I know how to check my own air filter, okay? My dad taught me that when I was sixteen. He had this old Chevy truck... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, making mistakes. No, I don't really do that. I'm pretty sharp when it comes to the work stuff. I just can't sit still while I'm doing it.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others when they're talking, or blurting things out before they finish speaking?

Yeah, I definitely do that. I mean, it's almost like a reflex. If I'm walking through the precinct or something, and I hear the junior detectives discussing a lead, I just jump right in. I'll start firing off questions or giving them advice before they even ask me, or before they finish their sentence. And then afterward, I'm like, wow, I completely barged into their conversation. Or even at home, if my neighbor is in the hallway talking to someone else... oh, my neighbor, Mrs. Gable, she has this little Yorkie that just barks at everything. And she dresses it up in these tiny sweaters. Last week it was wearing a miniature trench coat, which I thought was hilarious given my line of work. I asked her where she got it, and she said she knits them herself. Can you imagine having the patience to sit and knit a tiny trench coat? I would lose my mind. I tried knitting once in college because my roommate was super into it, but I just ended up with this weird, lumpy scarf that looked like a giant caterpillar. 

Anyway, yeah, I'll hear Mrs. Gable talking about the building maintenance or something, and I just interject my opinion before I even realize what I'm doing. It's like the thought is in my head and it just has to come out right that second.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms of restlessness, inability to stay seated, interrupting others, and difficulties with impulse control strongly point to ADHD (F90.0). Other conditions like F43.0 (Acute Stress Reaction), F32.0 (Mild Depressive Episode), F20.0 (Schizophrenia, Paranoid Type), and F60.3 (Borderline Personality Disorder) have been ruled out due to lack of supporting symptoms such as mood episodes, psychotic features, or significant emotional dysregulation/identity disturbance.
